title: Part 1: What Not to Do Before You Start Writing Your College Essay
excerpt: Getting started on your personal statement? Before you write a single word, make sure you’re not accidentally setting yourself up for stress later on. At Blue Stars, we’ve seen that the most…

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Getting started on your personal statement? Before you write a single word, make sure you’re not accidentally setting yourself up for stress later on.

At Blue Stars, we’ve seen that the most compelling essays start with strategy, not just inspiration. That’s why we guide students through key decisions before the writing even begins—like how to interpret prompts, choose the right topic, and think about their overall story across all application materials.

Here are the most common pitfalls to avoid—and what to do instead—before you write:

ON PROCESS — Prep & Planning

❌ DON’T ✅ DO
Skip reading the prompt (even if you think you are already familiar with it) before brainstorming. Read each prompt carefully, marking it up to make sure you are answering the question(s) asked.
Decide on a topic for one essay without considering the full array of essays for each application. Plan your topics strategically. Consider the themes of all your essays before deciding on a topic for your Common App Personal Statement.
Get too much help from others. Everyone will have different opinions about what you should write. Stay true to your voice. Seek feedback, but ensure the final essay reflects your authentic self. A fresh perspective is often better than advice from those who know you too well.
Stress over whether your topic is “good enough.” Choose meaningful topics. What matters most is how you explore the topic, its impact on you, and what you learned.
Overanalyze “successful” essay examples. Draw inspiration carefully. Focus on telling your own unique story in a way that is true to you.

 Once you’ve laid the foundation, it’s time to tackle the writing. But even strong starts can veer off course without careful attention to tone, detail, and structure. That’s where Part 2 comes in.

title: Elite Summer Internships and Programs You Don't Want Your Child to Miss
excerpt: If you are interested in a unique internship for your child aligned with what top schools expect, get in touch with us to talk about summer planning!

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Can you picture your teen as a Business Development Intern at a Harvard/Wharton-founded venture firm creating a new credit card? This is exactly what a Blue Stars student did last summer and continues to do virtually now that the semester has started.

Or maybe your child wants to join a coding team for a UN-backed startup founded by UC Berkeley and University of Waterloo alumni who are building a gamified adaptive learning interface to accelerate youth learning in developing countries. Another Blue Stars student was lucky enough to secure this global tech opportunity.

Perhaps a chance to work with MIT graduates and NASA engineers on AI-powered medical-grade air purifiers might seem exciting to your college-bound student.

This is just a small sampling of the exciting, elite opportunities Blue Stars finds for families!

Over the years, Dr. M and her team have built a special collection of exclusive partnerships with industry colleagues who provide state-of-the-art, hands-on opportunities for students to gain impressive experiences, build their resumes, and strengthen their case for admission to a top college.

If you are interested in a unique internship for your child aligned with what top schools expect, get in touch with us to talk about summer planning!

Elite summer programs, too, can help lead to top school admission. In fact, no matter what your child is doing over the summer, as long as they are engaged in what they love, are productive, and learn from their experiences, your child will be well on the way to a great school.

In today’s highly competitive college admissions landscape, simply excelling in the classroom is not enough. Top-tier institutions are consistently looking for students who demonstrate initiative, depth of interest, and real-world experience in their chosen fields. This goes beyond the standard high school curriculum and enters the realm of specialized endeavors, like internships and academic summer programs.

For a student aspiring to major in a specific area or pursue a particular career, engaging in an internship or deep academic exploration during the summer can be a game-changer. Not only does it provide a practical understanding of the field, but it also signals to colleges that the student is deeply committed, proactive, and ready to contribute to their campus community from day one. Such experiences highlight a student’s dedication and can set them apart in a sea of talented applicants.

Some of the pre-college programs we’re particularly impressed by are:

  • 1

    Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS) – EA deadline of 11/1: A globally diverse, two-week summer program that unites over 2,000 students from 150+ countries and all 50 U.S. states, fostering collaboration on innovative topics and providing a unique international perspective.

  • 2

    COSMOS – This flagship program offers a wide range of clusters in courses ranging from science, technology, engineering, and mathematics subjects where talented and motivated students have the opportunity to work with renowned faculty, researchers, and scientists in state-of-the-art facilities while exploring advanced STEM topics far beyond the courses usually offered in California high schools.

  • 3

    Wharton Data Science Academy – The ultimate summer experience for students engaged in or passionate about data science, equipping them with crucial skills, while also fostering proficiency in the R language, favored by professional data scientists across academia and industry.

  • 4

    B-BAY – Students learn from UC Berkeley faculty and mentors, combining online classes, independent research, lab work, and team projects, culminating in the development and presentation of an original business plan.

  • 5

    Penn The Neuroscience Research Academy – Led by Penn’s experts, the Academy delves into the biological underpinnings of the brain, from neurons to cognitive functions, offering insights into mind and health in a residential program.

  • 6

    University of Chicago RIBS – An immersive four-week program where students gain hands-on experience in molecular, microbiological, and cell biology techniques, developing vital skills for future research endeavors, all in a dynamic lab environment.

  • 7

    Sci|Art UCLA – In the dynamic Sci|Art Studio + Lab, students embark on a transformative two-week journey fusing the worlds of science and art while also honing analytical and creative prowess to forge a solid foundation for interdisciplinary thinking before their undergraduate pursuits.

  • 8

    RISD – Rising high school juniors and seniors immerse themselves in a transformative five-week experience, follow a college-level curriculum in day-long studio classes, collaborate with creative peers from around the world, and gain access to renowned resources, ultimately redefining their approach to art and design.

  • 9

    SSP – Provides hands-on experience in experimental science for high school students, fostering teamwork, research, and lifelong connections, with 2023 marking the operation of six diverse programs in Astrophysics, Biochemistry, and Genomics, all celebrated as ‘the educational experience of a lifetime’ by its passionate alumni.

  • 10

    BU Rise – This six-week immersive program, offers an opportunity for students with a deep passion for science to engage in hands-on laboratory research under the guidance of distinguished mentors, or to delve into structured group research in the field of computational neurobiology.

These are just a sample of the elite internships and summer programs available to you because of Blue Stars’ special relationships with premier partners. You can explore some inspiring success stories from our alumni here.

If you’re ready to plan a summer experience that aligns with what top schools expect, contact our experts for personalized assistance in summer planning!

title: The SAT is Back: What College-Bound Teens and Their Parents Need to Know
excerpt: For the past few years, the SAT has seemed to fade into the background, with many colleges embracing test-optional policies. But the tide is turning. From MIT to Yale, Dartmouth to Brown, a growing number of top-tier schools have reinstated the SAT requirements, citing data that standardized tests can provide valuable insights into academic readiness and help level the playing field. If you're the parent of a high-performing student, understanding the evolving testing landscape is crucial. The SAT isn't just making a comeback—with the exception of the UC system, it’s regaining ground as a key component in the admissions process and […]

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
For the past few years, the SAT has seemed to fade into the background, with many colleges embracing test-optional policies. But the tide is turning. From MIT to Yale, Dartmouth to Brown, a growing number of top-tier schools have reinstated the SAT requirements, citing data that standardized tests can provide valuable insights into academic readiness and help level the playing field.

If you’re the parent of a high-performing student, understanding the evolving testing landscape is crucial. The SAT isn’t just making a comeback—with the exception of the UC system, it’s regaining ground as a key component in the admissions process and a strategic tool for students aiming to stand out.

Why Are Colleges Reinstating the SAT?

At the forefront of this movement is MIT, whose research led them to conclude that SAT scores significantly improve the ability to assess student promise, especially those from under-resourced backgrounds. Here’s the takeaway:

  • Academic Predictability: Standardized test scores remain a valuable tool in assessing a student’s readiness for the academic rigor of top-tier institutions. For example, when MIT reviewed the performance of students admitted during their test-optional period, they found that SAT and ACT scores were strong indicators of who would do well, especially in demanding subjects like math and science. Without these scores, their ability to predict student success significantly declined, leading the institution to reinstate its testing requirement.
  • Equity and Access: While critics often argue that standardized testing favors wealthier students, many colleges and education researchers now point to the role that these tests play in uncovering hidden talent. Students from under-resourced schools may not have access to AP classes, elite tutoring, or extracurricular opportunities that enhance college applications, but a high standardized test score can help them stand out. Additionally, free resources like Khan Academy’s SAT practice (developed in partnership with the College Board) offer equitable test prep access, helping level the playing field regardless of income or background. A 2017 study by the College Board and Khan Academy found that 20 hours of practice on the platform was associated with an average 115-point score increase.

Institutions like Dartmouth, Yale, and Brown echoed this perspective. In fact, Dartmouth economists revealed that many low-income students chose not to submit scores, even when their results were strong, incorrectly believing the scores wouldn’t help. As it turns out, these students may have actually hurt their chances by withholding valuable information. The data showed that submitting scores increased their likelihood of admission by more than threefold.

The Test-Optional Landscape: Where Are We Now?

Despite the SAT’s return at many elite schools, the broader college admissions world remains a mixed bag. While hundreds of colleges still maintain test-optional policies, “optional” doesn’t mean “irrelevant.”

Here’s the nuance: submitting strong scores can still offer a competitive advantage. Colleges may say they evaluate applicants equally, but behind the scenes, test scores are often used to:

  • Interpret transcripts from unfamiliar high schools 
  • Identify standout students in lower-resourced communities 
  • Offset a lower GPA 
  • Predict academic performance more accurately than any other component of the application

And since some schools still offer merit scholarships based on SAT/ACT scores, it could lead to money that could make a meaningful difference in your family’s college financial planning.

Why High-Achieving Students Should Still Take the SAT

If your student is aiming for selective or highly selective colleges, taking the SAT (or ACT) is a smart move. Here’s why:

  • A Competitive Edge: Strong scores reinforce academic excellence, especially for students applying from highly resourced schools or districts. 
  • Scholarship Opportunities: Many institutions tie merit-based aid to test scores. 
  • Admissions Signal: Submitting a score, particularly when it’s above a school’s median, can signal strength and seriousness to admissions officers. 
  • Context Matters: A test score that’s not “perfect” may still be above average for a student’s school or neighborhood, which admissions teams consider. 

Remember: not submitting a score may be interpreted differently based on your student’s context. For example, students from affluent areas or private schools are often expected to submit strong scores. Not doing so might send the wrong signal.

What’s New with the SAT?

In March 2023, the SAT fully transitioned to a digital format, marking the biggest change to the exam in its history. Here’s what families need to know:

  • Shorter Testing Time: The digital SAT is about two hours instead of three. 
  • Adaptive Format: How students perform on the first half of each section determines the difficulty of the second half, making early performance critical. 
  • Faster Scores: Results come back in days, not weeks. 
  • New Tools: Students take the test through the Bluebook app, which includes built-in calculators, annotation tools, and timing features. 

If your student hasn’t yet taken a digital SAT, it’s important to practice specifically for this new format to avoid surprises on test day.

Quick Tips for SAT Success

Whether your student is taking the SAT for the first time or looking to boost a previous score, strategic preparation matters:

title: 4 Key Differences Between Computer Science and Data Science Majors
excerpt: Not sure whether to guide your child toward a major in computer science or data science? You're not alone in this dilemma

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Not sure whether to guide your child toward a major in computer science or data science?

You’re not alone in this dilemma, as these two fields are becoming increasingly popular because of their extensive usefulness in our digital age, promising a wide range of job opportunities and potential for innovation.

Let’s delve into the four main differences between these majors, so you can better guide your student in making the right choice.

1. Core Focus

At the heart of Computer Science (CS) is the study of algorithms, computation, and information theory. The CS major focuses on creating computer systems that can perform tasks efficiently and effectively, from mobile apps and operating systems, to designing complex networks and databases.

Data Science (DS), on the other hand, focuses on extracting insights from vast amounts of data. It combines disciplines like statistics, data analysis, and machine learning to interpret, predict, and leverage data to inform decision-making.

2. Skillset

While there’s some overlap, the core skills required in each field are distinct. In Computer Science, students dive deep into programming, system design, and algorithmic thinking. They must understand how to optimize system performance and solve complex computational problems.

In contrast, a Data Science student spends more time exploring statistical models, predictive algorithms, and data visualization tools. Their work revolves around turning raw data into meaningful insights, which requires both statistical acuity and a knack for storytelling.

3. Application

Both fields have broad applications, but they tend to focus on different areas. Computer Science graduates often work on designing and developing software applications, operating systems, and computing technology.

Data Scientists, however, are more likely to find themselves in roles that involve analyzing and interpreting complex digital data to help businesses make strategic decisions. They work across fields as diverse as healthcare, finance, retail, and government, uncovering trends and guiding policy or business strategy.

4. Career Prospects

Computer Science graduates have a vast range of potential job titles, from Software Developer, Systems Analyst, Network Architect, to IT Project Manager. Their skills are fundamental to virtually every industry in our digital world.

Data Science, being a relatively new and fast-growing field, has its own set of promising career prospects. These range from Data Analyst, Data Scientist, to Business Intelligence Analyst. With businesses increasingly driven by data, the demand for professionals who can make sense of this information is skyrocketing.

Conclusion

While both Computer Science and Data Science offer vibrant career paths, they each require a unique blend of skills and interests. If your high schooler enjoys problem-solving, programming, and system design, a major in Computer Science could be a great fit. If they are more interested in numbers, statistical patterns, and using data to tell a story, Data Science could be the perfect pathway.

Remember, there’s no one-size-fits-all answer when it comes to choosing the right major. Each student is unique, with their own talents, interests, and aspirations.

The journey towards college and career readiness can seem daunting, but it’s also a time of exciting possibilities. With understanding and encouragement, you can help your student unlock their potential and prepare for a future full of opportunity.

title: Acing UC Personal Insight Question 7 –  Your Community Impact
excerpt: UC Personal Insight Question 7 provides the perfect opportunity to show your commitment to making a positive impact on your environment

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“What have you DONE to make your school or your community a better place?”

Top schools like those in the UC system increasingly seek students who are not merely concerned with their own individual success but spend a great deal of time and attention solving real-world problems. The more students can show themselves to be active problem solvers, the more attractive they are to UC admissions readers.

UC Personal Insight Question 7 provides the perfect opportunity to show your commitment to making a positive impact on your environment, highlight your problem-solving skills, and dazzle your UC dream schools with your altruistic mindset.

Tip 1: Structure Your Essay in this Order: Problem, Solution, Wisdom

Your essay should follow a structured narrative that captures the essence of your community impact. Start by identifying the problem you encountered within your chosen community. Clearly articulate the challenges and issues that prompted you to take action.Next, describe the solution or actions you initiated to address this problem. Finally, conclude your essay with insightful wisdom gained from your experience. community impact.

Tip 2: Pick One Community and One Problem That You Focused On Addressing

Before delving into your essay, it’s essential to realize that “community” can extend far beyond your immediate surroundings. It can encompass your school, hometown, virtual groups, teams, and more. The key is to identify a problem within your chosen community that you aimed to address. This problem will be the driving force for your essay, allowing you to showcase your role as a problem solver.

Tip 3: Make Sure Your Reader Can Picture the Action or Activity

The core of your essay should focus on the actions you took to address the identified problem. Simply holding a title or membership is insufficient. Instead,vividly portray your proactive approach and efforts to effect change.

Tip 4: Detail What You Did to Help, How You Did It, and the Tangible Results of Your Work

Detailing the methods you employed to address the problem provides a vivid picture of your initiative. Make your reader feel like they are watching a movie unfold as they follow your journey.

  • Quantify the impact of your actions wherever possible. Describe the positive outcomes that resulted from your efforts. Did recycling rates increase? Were relationships between seniors and students strengthened? Tangible results validate your initiative and demonstrate your ability to create meaningful change.
  • While your actions are crucial, your response should also provide insight or wisdom gained from the experience. Reflect on the significance of your actions and how they contribute to creating a better community. Consider the implications of your efforts and how they align with your personal growth and values.

Tip 5: Avoid Simply Listing Your Quantifiable Volunteer Stats Such as Hours Logged

Your essay is not the place to list your volunteer hours or titles held. Instead, focus on a single, meaningful experience that highlights your dedication to improving your community. This allows you to go deeper into the specifics of your actions and their impact.

Tip 6: Edit Out Cliche Conclusions Such as “Now I Feel So Lucky for Everything I Have.”

One common pitfall to avoid in your UC Personal Insight Question 7 essay is using cliché conclusions. Admissions readers have seen these sentiments repeatedly, and they don’t provide valuable insight into your character or your contribution to your community.

Instead of resorting to clichés, strive to end your essay with a conclusion that is unique and genuinely reflects your experiences and growth. Consider the broader impact of your actions on your community and the valuable lessons you’ve learned along the way. Your conclusion should tie back to the central theme of your essay, emphasizing how your efforts have made a meaningful difference.

Crafting a compelling response to UC Personal Insight Question 3 involves identifying a problem, describing your actions, showcasing results, offering insight, and avoiding resume-style listing. By focusing on a meaningful initiative, you can showcase your proactive spirit and dedication to making your school or community a better place.

title: UC Personal Insight Question 6: Showcasing Your Academic Passion
excerpt: UC Personal Insight Question 6, or PIQ 6, provides the best opportunity for applicants to showcase all of their “fit-to-major” activities

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“Think about an academic subject that inspires you. Describe how you have furthered this interest inside and/or outside of the classroom.”

Personal Insight Question 6, or PIQ 6, provides the best opportunity for applicants to showcase all of their “fit-to-major” activities to make the case for their chosen course of study. It is especially important for students who select the same major across all campuses they apply to. It is vital for applicants to UC Berkeley’s engineering and business programs.

Unlike other UC prompts that offer creative interpretation, PIQ 6 is precise and focused. It revolves around an academic subject that inspires you. This prompt challenges applicants to delve deep into their academic passions and demonstrate how they’ve pursued their interests inside and outside the classroom.

In this blog post, we’ll guide you through crafting an exceptional response to this prompt by following eight essential tips. Download our complete guide for examples and a bonus introduction!

  • 1

    Embrace Everything Connected to Your Academic Passion: Think broadly about your chosen academic subject. If it’s biology, consider not only your coursework but also projects, assignments, clubs, summer programs, internships, research, volunteering, reading and/or viewing, and related experiences.

  • 2

    Identify Why You Love the Subject: Addressing why you’re drawn to the academic subject is crucial. What about it excites and inspires you? Whether it’s the analytical challenges of physics or the creative possibilities of literature, share what fuels your passion.

  • 3

    Use the Essay to Focus on Your Intended Major: PIQ 6 can serve as an anchor for your application, providing a central theme that aligns with your intended major. This essay is an opportunity to demonstrate your commitment to your chosen field of study.

  • 4

    Brainstorm Extensively: Cast a wide net during brainstorming. List every academic and extracurricular activity connected to your subject, even if it seems insignificant initially. This comprehensive list will serve as your “raw material.”

  • 5

    Choose an Organizational Approach: Decide whether to organize your content chronologically or thematically. Each approach has its merits. Chronological organization can show growth, while thematic organization can highlight different dimensions of your interest.

  • 6

    Stitch Together Your Content with Transitions: Assemble your essay by transitioning smoothly between different aspects of your involvement. Transition words, phrases, and clauses will help guide readers through your narrative.

  • 7

    Revise Diligently: Draft a detailed essay, and then trim it down to meet the word count. Don’t hesitate to revise several times to refine your narrative, eliminate redundancy, and ensure clarity and impact.

  • 8

    Ensure Harmony with Other Essays: Your UC application includes multiple essays, so ensure that your response to Personal Insight Question 6 complements your other essays. They should collectively provide a well-rounded picture of you as an applicant.

For winning examples and a bonus general introduction to tackling the UC Personal Insight Questions, download our complete guide below. We hope it inspires fresh ideas for your UC application!

Remember, the key is to demonstrate genuine passion, reflect on why the subject inspires you, and provide a clear and engaging narrative that complements your other essays. By following the eight tips outlined in this blog post, you can create a response to Personal Insight Question 6 that stands out and reflects the unique qualities that make you a strong candidate for admission to your desired UC campus.

title: Navigating Challenges and Thriving Academically: Answering UC Personal Insight Question 5
excerpt: UC Personal Insight Question 5 provides you with the unique opportunity to not only narrate a pivotal moment in your life but also to showcase your growth

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“Describe the most significant challenge you have faced and the steps you have taken to overcome this challenge. How has this challenge affected your academic achievement?”

When it comes to crafting a compelling personal statement for your college application, the prompts you encounter are your canvas to paint a vivid picture of who you are. Among these prompts, one stands out as an opportunity for introspection and vulnerability: describing a challenge that you faced and how it affected your achievement academically.

Master every UC PIQ essay challenge with our comprehensive guide. Fill out the form below to unlock the proven tips and tricks for guaranteed success!

This essay provides you with the unique opportunity to not only narrate a pivotal moment in your life but also to showcase your growth, resilience, and ability to triumph over adversity.

So how do you write about your greatest challenge in life in a way that makes you and your story shine? Here are six tips to ensure a winning essay.

1. Define the Significant Challenge Clearly

For your essay to be successful, it is important to be specific about what the challenge was and how it affected you. Being more specific helps you share your experience and efforts on a more intimate, and therefore impactful level.

2. Significant Doesn’t Have to Mean “Monumental”

When approaching the task of describing your most significant challenge, it’s crucial to recognize that significance is a deeply personal concept. The impact of an experience doesn’t solely rely on its grandeur or how it appears to others, so don’t feel compelled to conjure up a monumental event just for the sake of impressing admissions committees. Instead, emphasize the personal resonance of the challenge in your life. By shifting the focus from external perceptions to your internal journey, you allow your authentic self to shine through, capturing the essence of what truly matters in the narrative of your personal statement.

3. Connect the Challenge to Academic Achievement

While narrating your challenge, it’s important to seamlessly link it to your academic journey.

4. Outline the Steps Taken: Explain the “How”

The heart of your essay lies in discussing the steps you took to overcome the challenge. This is where the “how” comes into play. Whether you sought help, revamped your approach, set new goals, or found valuable resources, this section showcases your problem-solving skills and determination. This part of your essay is arguably the most important part of your story.

5. Structure Your Story as a “Triumph Sandwich”

We love to tell our students to think of any hardship story in terms of a “triumph sandwich.” When you write about hardship, you don’t want to start your story with the tough stuff because it won’t necessarily keep your readers attention. This structure adds a dynamic flow to your narrative that can be very enjoyable for your weary admissions essay reader!

6. Showing Vulnerability

Embrace vulnerability in your essay. Admissions officers value honesty and authenticity. This authenticity makes your essay memorable and impactful.

Crafting an essay that narrates your significant challenge and its impact on your academic journey can be a transformative process. By following the structure of the “triumph sandwich,” focusing on the “how,” and infusing your narrative with vulnerability and authenticity, you’ll create a powerful essay that not only answers the prompt but also highlights your resilience and personal growth. Remember, the story you share can make a lasting impression on admissions officers and help you stand out among applicants.

title: Answering UC Personal Insight Question 4: Educational Barriers or Opportunities
excerpt: UC Personal Insight Question 4 is a pivotal opportunity for applicants to share a meaningful story that showcases their personal growth and development

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“Describe how you have taken advantage of a significant educational opportunity or worked to overcome an educational barrier you have faced.”

As an academic institution, UC is curious about a student’s educational experience, and in this prompt they present applicants with a choice – to talk about an opportunity or a barrier in their educational journey. So, before you start to write this essay, we suggest you decide which path you want to take in crafting your story. Is it about an opportunity, or is it about a barrier?

Below you will find guidelines on both options. Remember, too, that “education” can be understood broadly and creatively. Maybe an AP class blew your mind, or perhaps your grandma imparted precious wisdom while teaching you how to make a favorite family dish. It all counts!

Personal Insight Question 4 is a pivotal opportunity for applicants to share a meaningful story that showcases their personal growth and development in the context of education. Let’s take a closer look at how to approach each aspect of the question.

Option 1: Seizing a Significant Educational Opportunity

When reflecting on a significant educational opportunity, consider experiences such as summer research, academic summer programs, independent projects, internships, volunteering, or cultivating special friendships. These experiences have the potential to greatly enhance your academic journey and personal development. As you craft your essay, remember to:

  1. Be Specific: Provide vivid details about the opportunity you seized, the goals you pursued, and the impact it had on your learning and personal growth.
  2. Highlight Growth: Describe how the experience challenged you, pushed your boundaries, and contributed to your development as a student and individual.
  3. Reflect on Impact: Discuss the ways in which this opportunity has influenced your academic and personal goals, and how you plan to carry its lessons forward.

Option 2: Overcoming an Educational Barrier

If you choose to address an educational barrier, you can draw from experiences like improving grades in a challenging class, excelling academically while dealing with a learning difference, navigating a lack of resources at your school, or learning in a foreign language. To effectively navigate this aspect of the prompt, follow these steps:

  1. Begin Positively: Start by setting the stage with a positive outlook, emphasizing your determination to overcome the barrier.
  2. Share the Hardship: Briefly describe the educational barrier you faced, focusing on its impact on your academic journey.
  3. Triumph and Growth: Dive into the strategies you employed to conquer the challenge, detailing your resilience, adaptability, and any support you sought.
  4. End on a Positive Note: Conclude by reflecting on how overcoming this barrier has transformed your perspective on education and your own capabilities.

Focus on What has Shaped your Academic Journey: UC Personal Insight Question 4 presents an opportunity to share a pivotal educational experience that has shaped your academic journey. Whether you choose to focus on a significant educational opportunity or an educational barrier you’ve overcome, remember that the admissions committee is interested in understanding your growth, resilience, and unique perspective. Craft a compelling essay that authentically conveys your experiences, lessons learned, and aspirations. As you navigate the writing process, keep in mind the tips provided in this guide and embrace the opportunity to showcase the depth of your character and the impact of your experiences.

title: Decoding UC Personal Insight Question 3: Six Tips for Writing About Your Greatest Talent or Skill
excerpt: So you've come across UC Personal Insight Question 3, which asks about your "greatest" talent or skill

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“What would you say is your greatest talent or skill? How have you developed and demonstrated that talent over time?”

So you’ve come across UC Personal Insight Question 3, which asks about your “greatest” talent or skill, and now you might be thinking, “How do I talk about my skills without sounding like I’m bragging?” or “Do I even have a ‘greatest’ talent?”

We get it, it’s a tricky one. But it’s important to remember that this prompt is less about the grandiosity of the skill and more about the journey of developing that talent or skill. In other words, this question isn’t just about what you’re good at, but more about your journey of getting better at it. And trust us, every skill, no matter how big or small, has its own awesome story.

We’re here to guide you on how to share that story in the best way possible. Ready? Let’s dive in!

1. Focus on the “over time” part of the prompt

Your UC admissions reader is especially interested in the progress you’ve made during your high school years. The admissions team is particularly interested in seeing how you’ve grown throughout your high school years. Have you been developing a particular talent or skill for two or more years during high school? If so, this is a solid foundation. The crucial part is to highlight the ‘over time’ aspect, illustrating the progress and growth in your chosen skill or talent. But remember, it’s not just about the length of time you’ve committed to an activity; it should be something significant that contributes to your profile.

2. Don’t forget the “how”

Most teens like to focus on “what” they did with this talent or skill. But the question isn’t really about your greatest talent or skill; it’s about your journey developing it. How did you hone your talent? Did you attend special classes, dedicate hours to practice, or find mentors? This essay is a process essay, essentially a narrative about the development of your talent or skill.

3. Don’t forget the “why”

The ‘why’ helps provide context to your journey. Why does this skill matter to you? And why should it matter to your admissions officer?

4. Your talent or skill can fall into any category

Your chosen talent or skill can be virtually anything, whether it is connected to STEM, humanities, art, a personal matter (making omelets, for example), or even something seemingly trivial. You can also delve into soft skills like listening or community building. Your skill or talent could likewise be a hobby you enjoy in your spare time or something directly related to your intended field of study. The UC system appreciates a diverse range of talents and skills.

5. Delve into “the mechanics” of the development

Discussing the fine details of your skill development is like opening the hood of a car to reveal the engine. It’s about showing the intricacies and details of how you cultivated your talent.

6. Don’t worry about being boring

Many applicants worry about their essay sounding dull. However, remember that this is a process essay. Your uniqueness shines through the ‘how’ and the ‘why.’ Even if you believe your talent or skill is common, your personal journey with it is uniquely yours. Trust in yourself and your way of going about things. Your reader is truly interested in your individuality.

To wrap up, remember that every person’s path of advancement in a talent or skill is unique, and it’s your story to tell. Even seemingly small passions can shine in this essay if they’ve played a significant role in your personal or academic development. So go ahead, start drafting, and remember, it’s your passion and dedication to your talent or skill that will truly make your essay stand out.

title: UC Personal Insight Question 2 on Creativity – Six Helpful Tips!
excerpt: Responding to UC Personal Insight Question 2 (PIQ2) can feel dizzying.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“Every person has a creative side, and it can be expressed in many ways: problem-solving, original and innovative thinking, and artistically, to name a few. Describe how you express your creative side.”

Responding to UC Personal Insight Question 2 (PIQ2) can feel dizzying. Many students find themselves wondering how to distill their multifaceted creative experiences into a focused and compelling essay.

Others read this prompt and immediately think: “But I’m not creative!” Don’t worry, that’s a common reaction, and it’s also likely not true. Everyone is creative in their own ways.

Whether you’re a STEM student exploring the intricate realms of coding or a humanities enthusiast crafting eloquent poetry, remember that creativity knows no boundaries. It’s all about embracing your individuality and leveraging your unique experiences.

Now, let’s dive into these six helpful tips to tackle UC PIQ 2 on creativity and create an essay that truly stands out.

  • 1

    Focus on Your Actual Creativity, Problem Solving, Innovative Thinking: A common mistake students make is leaning too heavily on “symbols” of creativity, such as being part of a drama club or orchestra. Instead of relying on your association with a club to tell the story, focus on a dramatic scene or complicated musical piece you mastered. Beyond commonly understood artistic activities, however, you could also demonstrate your genuine creativity, problem-solving skills, and innovative thinking in real-life situations. For winning examples and a bonus general introduction to tackling the UC Personal Insight Questions, download our complete guide below. We hope it inspires fresh ideas for your UC application!

  • 2

    Focus on One Example: Avoid being too broad or generic. Pick one specific example that represents your creativity. It could be a project you worked on, an initiative you took, or an innovative solution you came up with. Download our complete guide for examples and a bonus introduction!

  • 3

    Write about the “How” or Process: Describe the path you followed to manifest your creativity. This shows your thought process and how you approach problems. Discuss the hurdles you encountered and how you overcame them.

  • 4

What prompted you to think outside the box? This will give admissions officers an insight into the motivation behind your creativity, which will give deeper insight into who you are.

title: Help Your Teen Overcome Back-to-School Stress: 6 Proven Tips
excerpt: It’s that time again for your teen to switch gears from summer fun to the more structured rhythm of high school schedules.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
It’s that time again for your teen to switch gears from summer fun to the more structured rhythm of high school schedules.

And with that switch comes stress about the pressures of tougher academic coursework, about fitting in, or the unpredictability of what a new school year brings.

As a parent, you’re in a prime position to help your high schooler navigate these choppy waters. Here are six tips to help your teen overcome back-to-school stress:

1. Establish a Routine

A consistent routine fosters a sense of security and predictability, two critical stress relievers. Before the school year begins, work with your teen to establish a reliable daily schedule, including time for homework, extracurricular activities, family time, and importantly, downtime for relaxation.

2. Promote Healthy Habits

Nutrition, exercise, and sleep significantly impact stress levels. Encourage your teenager to maintain a balanced diet, engage in regular physical activity, and get plenty of sleep. These habits will not only help manage stress but also contribute to their overall well-being and academic success.

3. Encourage Open Communication

Your teen might be reluctant to talk about their stress. Foster an open, non-judgmental space for conversations. Let them know that it’s okay to feel anxious and that you’re always available for a chat, without offering immediate solutions or dismissals. Sometimes, being heard is all that’s needed.

Pro tip: have your teen’s favorite treats in the pantry and hang around the kitchen when they generally show up for snacks. They might be more open to talking if it feels casual and is accompanied by something delicious.

4. Teach Stress Management Techniques

Equip your teen with tools to handle stress independently. This can range from deep breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, and mindfulness techniques to hobbies that help them unwind. Encourage them to try different methods and adopt what works best for them.

5. Help Them Set Realistic Goals

High school brings an array of challenges that can seem overwhelming. Work with your teen to set achievable academic and personal goals. Emphasize the value of progress over perfection, encouraging them to strive for their best, not someone else’s.

6. Promote a Healthy Perspective

Reinforce the fact that everyone faces challenges and that they’re not alone in their struggles. Remind them that high school is just one phase of their life journey, and it’s okay to make mistakes along the way. It’s how they learn and grow.

Conclusion

These six strategies aren’t just for when school starts but can be integrated into your teen’s life year-round to mitigate stress. While you play a significant role, remember that your teenager is the one navigating their high school journey. Provide them with the tools, guidance, and support they need, but also give them room to develop resilience and problem-solving skills of their own.

In your supportive role, remember to take care of your well-being. A relaxed, well-nourished parent is far better equipped to guide their teenager through stressful periods. So, remember to breathe, stay balanced, and take time for self-care. By modeling healthy habits and maintaining a positive outlook, you’ll not only be looking out for your own well-being but also setting a powerful example for your teen. After all, the back-to-school journey is one you’re both navigating together – and with mutual support, it’s a journey that can lead to tremendous growth and success.

title: Responding to UC Personal Insight Question #1: Showcasing Leadership
excerpt: Are you ready to crack the UC Personal Insight Question #1 and showcase your leadership skills in an unforgettable essay?

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
“Describe an example of your leadership experience in which you have positively influenced others, helped resolve disputes or contributed to group efforts over time.”

Personal Insight Question (or PIQ) #1, or the “leadership” question, can feel like a hard puzzle for students. Our students often feel like they’ve contributed to the world around them but do not themselves identify as “leaders.” Other students feel they’ve done so much as leaders, they don’t know how to fit so much involvement into an essay of 350 words.

Well, for every puzzle, there is an opportunity! And at Blue Stars, we define every student who has contributed to the world around them as a leader and help them showcase their unique ways of taking initiative in their response to this tricky prompt.

So let’s see how any student who has made a positive difference can use this prompt to their own admission advantage!

First and foremost, before you do anything, your very first step is to read, dissect, and understand the prompt.

Understanding and dissecting the essay prompt: the importance of this step cannot be overstressed – it’s your guiding light throughout your essay-writing process. A beautifully crafted essay that answers the wrong question is a missed opportunity, potentially leaving the reader amused or, at worst, concerned about your attention to detail, and eligibility for their school.

For instance, in the context of PIQ #1, the essay prompt’s central theme is leadership, but a closer examination reveals it further specifies three different dimensions of leadership:

  1. Positively influencing others
  2. Resolving disputes, and
  3. Contributing to group efforts over time.

You are not required to address all three dimensions. Rather, you are encouraged to pick one area that you can explore in depth.

Even more interesting is the wording of the prompt, which suggests an inclusive and broad interpretation of leadership that goes beyond holding an official title or position in a club or organization. The focus here is not merely on the role you held but on how you actively contributed to group efforts and facilitated collaborative problem-solving. Therefore, a specific event or anecdote that clearly showcases one of the three aspects of leadership is what your University of California reader is looking for.

Now that you’ve studied the prompt, how do you write the essay? Here are 7 tips to help you brainstorm, organize, and evaluate your essay for effectiveness.

  • 1

    Select a specific event: Students should choose a particular event or project that highlights one of the three options in the prompt. Rather than presenting a list of activities, focusing on a single event allows for a deeper exploration of the applicant’s role and impact.

  • 2

    Go beyond formal organizational titles: We suggest an emphasis on contributions made and the positive effect on the group. Since your activities list already notes positions held in clubs or organizations, your collaborative problem-solving abilities or positive influence on group dynamics will more effectively demonstrate leadership skills in your essay.

  • 3

    Avoid martyr narratives: Applicants should avoid portraying themselves as the sole hero who single-handedly took charge. That model of leadership died in the 20th century. The 21st century is all about collaboration, which means that admissions readers these days are much more interested in how applicants worked with others to make a difference. In this essay, it’s important to highlight your ability to get things done effectively as part of a team.

  • 4

    Consider unconventional leadership interpretations: Traditional leadership roles aren’t the only way to showcase your abilities.

  • 5

    Maintain a balanced tone: Striking the right tone is vital. Be sure to include some humility while showcasing achievements and experiences, leaving a positive impression on your reader.

  • 6

    Showcase positive influence: One of the main aspects of this prompt is illustrating how your leadership positively influenced others. Discuss specific ways your actions made a difference and provide concrete examples of your impact. This could be the first part of your concluding paragraph, or upshot!

  • 7

    Demonstrate growth and reflection: Reflect on how this experience affected you as a leader and an individual, and discuss how it has shaped your leadership style and future goals. This could be the second part of the last paragraph, leaving your reader with an impression of a human being who constantly evolves, an important trait of any leader.

Ultimately, effective responses to UC PIQ #1 demand careful consideration and attention to detail. To be most successful, we encourage students to start early, allowing ample time for revisions. Remember, the UC essays are not just about the result but the process of personal growth and self-reflection. With the right approach, you can craft a standout essay that showcases your unique leadership qualities and contributes to a successful college application.

title: New Supplements are Coming in Response to SCOTUS Affirmative Action Decision!
excerpt: In light of the Supreme Court Decision to end affirmative action in college admissions, many students and families are wondering what they need to know.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
In light of the Supreme Court Decision to end affirmative action in college admissions, many students and families are wondering what they need to know.

Some colleges are in the midst of adding new supplemental essay questions designed to give additional space for students to discuss their identity and other factors that have shaped who they are.

We already know that Tufts University has added a new question “designed to provide…context about your lived experiences, the ideas and passions that excite you, and the ways in which you have shaped your communities.”

Sarah Lawrence has also written an additional question with an interesting spin, asking students to respond directly to the ruling itself. As of right now, we also know that Cornell, Rice, and Villanova will also be adding new supplemental essays (which have not been released yet).

What should applicants do in light of these changes? Hold tight until August 1, when the Common Application “rolls over” and this year’s admissions students can see if the schools on their list have added to or changed their prompts for the upcoming admissions cycle.

Of course, Blue Stars’ editors are here to help students navigate this latest shift in the admissions landscape with confidence. If you are curious about how to best tackle essay questions that relate to diversity and identity, sign up for your free Discovery Session today!

title: Tackling the Common Application Essay
excerpt: This blog post aims to provide you with valuable insights and tips to help you craft a successful Common Application Essay that will captivate the admissions officers and showcase your unique qualities.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Writing the Common Application essay can be a daunting task for high school students. However, with the right approach and guidance, you can craft an essay that stands out and effectively showcases your unique qualities and experiences.

This blog post aims to provide you with valuable insights and tips to help you craft a successful Common Application Essay that will captivate the admissions officers and showcase your unique qualities.

So, let’s dive in and explore what makes a Common Application essay stand out!

1. What Admissions Officers Look For

Before we delve into the tips for writing an exceptional Common Application Essay, let’s understand what admissions officers seek in these essays. Admissions officers want to see your personal growth and transformation through experiences. They are interested in understanding how you’ve evolved as an individual and what lessons you’ve learned along the way. The Common App essay is a personal narrative that should highlight your development.

2. Be Personal

Unlike in academic essays, this is not the occasion to showcase your knowledge of facts and figures. Admissions officers want to get to know you as a person, so make sure your essay reflects personal aspects of your life. Avoid writing in a formal tone; instead, be yourself and let your unique voice shine through!

3. Focus on Growth, Not Accomplishments

Remember that the Common App essay is not an opportunity to list your accomplishments and accolades. Those go in the Activities and Additional Information sections of your application. Instead, share your observations, reactions, and insights about the experiences that have shaped you. Admissions officers want to see introspection and self-awareness, not just a narrated list of achievements.

4. Show, Don’t Tell

When writing your Common App essay, aim to tell a story with cinematic sensory details. Take your readers on a journey by describing the setting, the time of day, the people involved, and the actions taking place. Feel free to incorporate dialogue and use real or fictional names. These details help anchor your reader in the story and make it more engaging.

5. Be Specific about Time

To provide context and structure to your essay, include specific moments or periods of time. Mention the grade you were in, your age at the time of the events, and the timeline between significant moments. This helps the reader understand the progression and impact of your experiences. Timestamps provide clarity and make your story more relatable.

6. Embrace Creativity (But It’s Not Required)

The Common Application Essay allows for creative expression, giving you the freedom to explore different writing styles and formats. You can take risks, be innovative, and infuse your essay with your artistic flair. However, remember that creativity is not a requirement. It’s more important to stay true to your own voice and write authentically. Don’t feel pressured to be creative if it doesn’t come naturally to you.

7. Structure Your Story for Impact

If you’re writing about a challenging or painful experience, consider using the “Triumph Sandwich” structure: start your essay with a positive introduction, delve into the difficult part in the middle, and conclude with the lesson learned or the positive change that occurred. This structure helps balance the emotional impact on the reader and leaves them with a hopeful and inspiring message.

8. Write in Your Own Voice

Your Common App essay should sound like you. Avoid trying to sound overly mature or sophisticated in your writing. Admissions officers want to hear your authentic voice and get a sense of who you are as an individual. Read your essay out loud or record yourself speaking to ensure it sounds natural.

9. Include Content Unavailable Elsewhere in the Application

While it’s acceptable to mention a particular experience in a club that you’ve also discussed in the activity essay, avoid duplicating the same information. Admissions readers expect to find something new about applicants – something they can’t find anywhere else in the application – when they read personal statements. Your application provides limited space for an applicant’s entire presentation, so make each aspect of it count.

10. Plan Your Essay Structure before You Start Writing

Each paragraph should have a clear purpose and contribute to the overall message of your essay. By organizing your thoughts and ideas before writing, you can ensure that each paragraph serves a specific role in advancing your narrative. The writing process will also be easier and more pleasant!

11. Draft More Than the Word Count

It’s easier to cut down an essay than it is to add more content. Get all of your ideas out to your satisfaction. Then make sure the draft matches the structure. Then start cutting the draft down. It will feel so good!

12. Seek Feedback

Once you have a rough draft, seek feedback from a trusted reader who can provide constructive criticism. Look for someone who can offer unbiased insights and identify any gaps in your ideas. Avoid seeking feedback from family members or close friends who may have an emotional attachment to your work.

13. Take a Break

After receiving feedback, take a day or two to let it sink in. Gain some distance from your essay. When you revisit your draft with fresh eyes, you’ll be better equipped to assess whether it accurately conveys your intended message.

14. Revise, Revise, Revise

Revision is a crucial part of the writing process. Embrace the idea of demolishing and rebuilding your essay, making bold changes where necessary. Be willing to revise multiple times until you are satisfied with the final draft.

15. Trim to Word Count

Now would be the time to cut down your draft to fit the specified word count by removing unnecessary adjectives, prepositional phrases, and repetitive clauses. Consider condensing lengthy sections into concise phrases. Using contractions can also help reduce word count.

16. Read Your Essay Out Loud a Few Times before Submitting

Reading your essay out loud will help you catch common proofreading errors such as “the the” or a missing word. After you’re confident the essay is error free, it’s time to submit it. Remember, the Common Application essay is an opportunity for you to showcase your unique qualities and experiences. With careful planning, thoughtful reflection, and revision, you can create an impactful essay that resonates with admissions officers. Good luck!

title: Vital to Impressing Top Colleges is Doing Deep School Research: We'll Show You How
excerpt: In this blog post, we will guide you through a step-by-step process to conduct effective school research and impress top colleges.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Choosing the right college is a crucial decision in every student’s life. With so many options available, it can be overwhelming to navigate the application process and stand out among thousands of other applicants. One underrated but essential part of the process is conducting deep school research. This research not only helps you make an informed decision about your college choices but also plays a vital role in crafting compelling application essays and showcasing your genuine interest in the institution. In this blog post, we will guide you through a step-by-step process to conduct effective school research and impress top colleges.

Step 1: Start with the Basics

When beginning your research, it’s important to explore the college’s official website. Navigate to the homepage and focus on three key sections: academics, research, and campus life. These sections provide valuable insights into the college’s offerings and help you understand if it aligns with your interests and goals.

Step 2: Explore Academics

Within the academics section of a university website, look for an “Explore Majors” page or a similar resource. Here, you can find detailed information about different majors and departments. If you have a specific area of interest, such as biology, delve deeper into the department’s webpage. Take note of the various specializations and concentrations available within the major. This information can help you narrow down your focus and develop a more specific academic angle.

Step 3: Dive into Course Offerings

To gain a deeper understanding of the curriculum, explore the list of courses offered by the department. Look for courses that align with your interests and goals. Get excited about the possibilities and explore different subjects within your chosen major. This exploration not only helps you make informed decisions but also demonstrates your enthusiasm and genuine interest in the field.

Step 4: Discover Faculty and Research Opportunities

Faculty members play a pivotal role in shaping your college experience. Explore the department’s faculty page to familiarize yourself with the professors and their areas of expertise. Take note of any research opportunities or labs that align with your interests. Research experience is highly valued by top colleges, so it’s essential to showcase your eagerness to engage in meaningful research within your field.

Step 5: Explore Extracurricular Opportunities

Beyond academics, colleges offer a range of extracurricular activities and clubs. These opportunities can enrich your college experience and provide avenues for personal and professional growth. Visit the campus life section of the college website to discover the diverse clubs, organizations, and service opportunities available. Take note of clubs or groups related to your specific interests, such as dance, entrepreneurship, or community service.

Step 6: Craft Your Essays

Armed with in-depth knowledge about the college, you can now tackle the application essays with confidence. Many colleges ask “Why” essays, where you need to explain why you are a good fit for the institution. These essays require more than generic answers. Utilize your research to demonstrate your understanding of the college’s unique offerings, such as specific courses, professors, or research opportunities. Showcase your passion and how the college can help you achieve your academic and personal goals.

Step 7: Tailor Your Application

Your application should reflect the depth of your research and alignment with the college’s values and culture. Highlight the specific programs, courses, or extracurricular activities that resonate with your interests and aspirations. Tailor your application to show why you are a perfect fit for the college and how you can contribute to its community.

Conclusion

Conducting deep school research is a crucial step in securing an edge in the college application process. It enables you to make informed decisions, demonstrate your genuine interest in the college, and craft compelling essays and applications. By following the steps outlined in this blog post, you will be well-equipped to impress top colleges with your knowledge and enthusiasm. Remember, the effort you invest in researching colleges today will pay off in the end with increased admissions success.

Our personalized approach leads to results that you might not have imagined when starting the process.

title: Fun Family Activities for Road Trips
excerpt: Below are activities and resources for parents and teens to explore together while enjoying summer fun!

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Summer vacation is a great opportunity to spend quality time together as a family. Whether you are planning a road trip, a weekend getaway, or international travel, there are plenty of fun things to do that can bring your family closer together through shared exploration.

Below are activities and resources for parents and teens to explore together while enjoying summer fun!

Check out the Blue Stars resources menu for blogs and videos on a wide range of college planning topics. Here are a few of our favorites!

  • Interview with Dr. Irena Smith Author of “The Golden Ticket: Life in College Admissions Essays”

  • Celebrating Your Child’s Unique Strengths – a conversation with Dr. Irena Smith

  • 5 College Admissions Tips for STEM students

  • Tackling the Common App Essay

Play games focused on conversation starters. The decks below ask open-ended questions designed to get everyone talking!

  • Talking College Cards | Andrea M. Brenner

  • The Hygge Conversation Game

  • Letz Talk Conversation Cards for Teens – Communication Topics, Conversation Starters – Build Confidence & Emotional Intelligence

Queue up a few podcasts for the car or plane ride! These are four that our students love!

  • In Machines We Trust | MIT Technology Review

  • Future of the Business World (Wharton Global Youth Program)

  • Lost Women of Science

  • The Gradient (on AI)

Listen to the latest fiction and non-fiction best-sellers! Klara and the Sun generated a lot of interesting conversations with our students and their counselors this year.

  • Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro

  • Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman

  • The Dawn of Everything by David Graeber, David Wengrow

  • Grit by Angela Duckworth

Pro Tip:

In addition to these ideas, try asking each family member to make their own playlist to share in the car! One of our students did this a few years ago with her family, and she ended up writing about the experience of sharing music on a roadtrip in one of her excellent supplemental essays for Brown University.

Once you’re at your destination, make sure to continue the conversation during activities like hiking to visiting a museum or historic site. Making summers both fun and educational for the whole family is something you won’t regret. You’ll create lasting memories and help your child grow personally, paving the way for an excellent, enriching admissions journey down the road.

Happy Summer! And have fun :)

title: The Blue Stars Difference
excerpt: Since founding Blue Stars in 2010, Dr. M has shaped a coaching methodology that serves as the backbone of all Blue Stars engagements, and she’s created a multi-year certification program for guiding her counseling team in its master practice.

author.name: Dr. Amy Morgenstern
author.bio: Dr. Amy Morgenstern ('Dr. M') founded Blue Stars in 2010. She holds a Ph.D. and MFA, and created 'The Calm Way' methodology to guide students to Ivy League and top-choice acceptances.

contentHtml:
Since founding Blue Stars in 2010, Dr. M has shaped a coaching methodology that serves as the backbone of all Blue Stars engagements, and she’s created a multi-year certification program for guiding her counseling team in its master practice. Besides her regular one-on-one meetings with each counselor, she and the team work collaboratively and collegially on a daily basis to support one another in executing (and improving) the Blue Stars methodology, which has fortified hundreds of college-bound students and led them to success in admissions for over a decade.

The core principles of the Blue Stars methodology include:

1. Personal growth leads the way.

It’s our motto. It’s our mantra. It’s our collective, deeply held belief. And, happily, it aligns with the expectations of elite colleges and universities, which not only recognize external accomplishments like grades but are intrigued by who a student is, from the inside out. Based on her training as a scholar of ancient Greek philosophy, Dr. M has created a mentorship style that centers individual actualization as the cornerstone of each teen’s unique journey to college. Key to her method is helping a student figure out their purpose (or “why”). As author and lecturer Leah Weiss states, “Purpose is an amazing superpower for resilience.” How true! Through our focus on activities that help a student define and activate who they are in a way that feels authentic to them, we see their resilience come to life in front of our eyes. Admissions readers see it, too!

2. Building life skills for now, college, and beyond.

So much stress can be created because teens feel overwhelmed by their academic workload and other demands while their brains are not yet developmentally equipped with the executive functions for the time-management required to succeed in today’s high school environment. A scholar of Aristotle, particularly his treatises on ethics, which she taught at the university level, Dr. M sees time management as a skill that needs to be patiently taught through repetition, just like learning to ride a bike, throw a pitch, play the piano, or be a good person. It takes practice. And it is understandable that parents may not have patience or time to work with teens in this painstaking but proven way. That’s where Blue Stars comes in. We teach students how to build time-management systems that work for them, and we troubleshoot with them as they stumble through their “training-wheel stage.” As they advance, Blue Stars students become productive, calm, and mature. By the time they apply to college, they, too, are amazed at how much they’ve accomplished over the years.

3. A culture of deep, open, nonjudgmental conversation and active integrated listening.

At Blue Stars, we take teens, their emotions, and their thought patterns very seriously, and we find ways to help them process life in their own way. Once a certain kind of pressure is lifted and students are given space to think and talk freely, it’s remarkable how good the outcome can be! Blue Stars counselors are truly interested in every person they meet and enjoy helping each student get in touch with their uniqueness. We believe that everyone needs to be heard and feel heard. The result is a tight-knit, trusting relationship between student and counselor, leading to best-fit results for each teen. In short, like Socrates and Plato, we find healthy, clarifying dialogue to be the first step toward effective action.

4. Where there is a teen, there are structured exercises leading to action plans.

In full agreement with University of Oregon child development specialist Dr. Nicholas Allen’s observation that, if a teen is given enough time for reflection, their decision-making skills “can be on-par with a fully-grown adult,” Dr. M has designed a mentorship style focused on helping students make good decisions for themselves. Taking into account the developmental stage of adolescents, she and her team have created numerous proprietary interactive exercises that provide step-by-step guidance in envisioning creative pathways to college and setting goals to achieve teens’ dreams. In our practice, we routinely navigate between free-flowing exploration and structure, structure, structure!

5. Driven by analytical thinking at every level of service.

A trained philosopher, seasoned researcher, and lifelong innovator, Dr. M loves systems, evidence, and data! Since the Great Recession, she’s presented on the topic “New Trends in Admissions” – noting how cultural shifts impact the admissions experience for applicants. A seasoned systematic strategist, Dr. M carefully observes American culture, admissions expectations, and teen psychology, studying how they shift and change over time, and then translates these new trends back into a coaching practice that comes to life through seasoned counselors who work closely with Dr. M, and one another.

6. Spirited by a growth mindset.

The Blue Stars team approaches all we do with a spirit of inquiry, curiosity, adaptability, and flexibility. We grow and change with the times, all the while focusing on providing maximum success for our students.

7. We believe in long-term relationships :)

There’s nothing better than talking with a high school senior about how much they’ve changed since ninth grade. Real growth needs time and investment, so Blue Stars strives to stay with our students throughout their entire educational journey. We don’t expect our students (or ourselves) to mature overnight, but when we look back at the end of all four years of high school, it’s incredible what has been accomplished!

Contact us today to see how we can make a difference for your student.
